newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia king says not to recognise Ung Huot as PM.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia king says not to recognise Ung Huot as PM.

text.p: Cambodian King Sihanouk said on Monday he would not recognise the appointment of Foreign Minister Ung Huot as First Prime Minister, saying the position belonged to ousted leader Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

"While maintaining my affection for him, I will abstain from giving His Excellency Mr Ung Huot his new title of 'first prime minister'; a title which, until his formal condemnation by an independent Khmer tribunal, ...Norodom Ranariddh has the right to retain," Sihanouk said in comments faxed to reporters.
The president of Cambodia's National Assembly called on Monday for Ung Huot to be approved as first prime minister in place of Ranariddh, overthrown in a bloody coup on July 6.
The call came despite a weekend announcement by Ranariddh that Ung Huot was being temporarily expelled from his royalist FUNCINPEC party.

The appointment of Ung Huot by an incomplete parliament would be invalid, Sihanouk said in an interview released by his cabinet to news agencies in Beijing, where he has been receiving medical treatment.

"The decisions of an incomplete parliament working under conditions of very questionable 'freedom' and 'regularity' could not be considered valid within the spirit of our 1993 Constitution and our liberal democracy," he said.
